children: Grain traders are taking cues from the estimates on U.S. crop size coming from private analysts this week, ahead of next week's WASDE report. Corn has the most riding on what analysts project ahead of the monthly USDA release, with corn generally more advanced in maturity than soybeans at this time of year. "The market is expecting StoneX's updated U.S. corn and soybean crop estimates this afternoon, followed by [AgResource] reportedly Thursday or Friday and S&P Global Energy on Friday," says Jim Wiesemeyer of Ag Bull Trading. "The succession of estimates could determine whether the recent rally has moved too far, too quickly or whether private forecasters increasingly validate the market's concern that USDA is still too high on corn yield." (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
